title: Opaque policy tag translation led to intermittent regional bounce - follow-up and action items
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity degradation event on 2026-03-09 we observed intermittent cross-region request bounce between us-west and eu-west for ~27 minutes. Symptoms: elevated 5xx/latency spikes for affected customers, <10% of requests experienced repeated reroutes (2-6 hops) before falling back to lower-tier model variants or timing out. Root cause investigation identified a logic gap in the policy translation layer: an internal 'opaque' policy tag used for trial routing (tag value 'trial-v2:opaque') was not included in the legacy precedence map. When the policy mesh synced a policy snapshot that referenced the opaque tag, routers in some regions treated the tag as unknown and applied a fallback policy that favored remote regions with a stale sticky-token TTL. The combination of sticky TTL misinterpretation and asynchronous policy propagation created a small window where requests bounced between regions as each side tried to honor a locally-considered-preferred route. Contributing factors: (1) policy-tag-translation path did not normalize unknown tags to a safe default; (2) sticky-route ttl was implemented as an optimistic local cache that could be overridden by remote preference without proper damping; (3) telemetry for 'variant-handoff' lacked a histogram of hop-count, making detection slower; (4) a recent change to the policy snapshot publisher increased propagation parallelism which amplified brief inconsistencies.
impact_timeline: 2026-03-09 14:03 UTC - First alert: elevated request latencies for models in us-west
2026-03-09 14:06 UTC - Automated autoscale triggered; small reduction in error rates
2026-03-09 14:09 UTC - Anomalous routing traces show requests with >1 cross-region hop
2026-03-09 14:12 UTC - Pager duty engaged; mitigation: temporarily increase local preference weight for us-west
2026-03-09 14:30 UTC - Policy snapshot rollback initiated for the trial tag; routing converged and incident resolved by 14:35 UTC
root_cause: Missing normalization of non-canonical policy tags combined with a sticky-route TTL semantics mismatch across regional routers. Unknown tags were converted to an implicit fallback that preferred remote region variants; simultaneous propagation of updated snapshots between regions created oscillation and repeated reroutes.
mitigations_applied_during_incident: Rolled back snapshot containing the experimental 'trial-v2' tag mapping
Increased local region preference weight as temporary isolation
Activated conservative routing gate (single-hop enforcement) for most customer tiers for 25 minutes
action_items: ENG-AI-01: Implement tag normalization in the policy translation pipeline — map unknown/opaque tags to an explicit 'unknown_safe' policy before snapshot generation (owner: Marco Nguyen, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-17)

ENG-AI-02: Add damping for sticky-route TTL updates — introduce a weighted backoff window (configurable) to prevent immediate override from remote preferences (owner: Sunita Rao, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-24)

ENG-AI-03: Extend routing telemetry — emit hop-count histogram, per-request policy-tag hash, and sticky-ttl-origin metadata to tracer and traces-aggregator (owner: Leo Martinez, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-18)

ENG-AI-04: Add regression test to policy-snapshot publisher verifying idempotent behavior with unknown tags and measured propagation order under parallel publish (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-19)

ENG-AI-05: Update runbook: include 'opaque-tag rollback' steps and add checklist to enforce canary validation of new tags for 30 minutes in single-region shadow before cross-region publication (owner: On-call Runbook Team, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-AI-06: Post-deploy telemetry audit — create a dashboard that alerts on average hop-count > 1.2 or >3% of requests with >1 reroute (owner: Data Infra, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-21)

ENG-AI-07: Review recent policy publisher change that increased parallelism and add a safe-guard throttle to prevent near-simultaneous multi-region snapshot application (owner: Rafael Gomez, estimate: 4, due: 2026-03-22)
ENG-AI-08: Customer outreach draft for affected tenants — communications, SLA credits, and summary of corrective actions (owner: Katelyn Brooks, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-16)
testing_and_validation: Will validate fixes in a staged environment with a synthetic routing mesh that simulates inconsistent propagation. Tests include: (1) unknown-tag normalization test scenarios; (2) sticky-ttl damping behavior under conflicting regional policies; (3) load test with high parallel snapshot publishes to assert no hop-count regression. Each test will be added to CI as a flake-resistant suite.

2026-03-11 16:40 - Marco Nguyen: Began implementation of tag normalization. Found that legacy snapshots still permit unset tags; adding translation layer at publisher is safest.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Priya Shah: Wrote unit tests that simulate unknown tags; they pass locally. Scheduling CI stress job to validate publish ordering.
2026-03-13 08:30 - Leah Brooks (PM): Confirmed customer outreach draft. Prioritizing ENG-AI-01 and ENG-AI-02 for next deploy window. Please add rollout plan and feature flag for tag normalization.
notes: This incident surfaced an interplay between policy authoring assumptions and runtime semantics. The most important long-term fix is defensive policy translation and stricter canaries for new tag types. Avoid global simultaneous snapshot publishing without cross-region quiesce/ack semantics. Consider a future design where policy tags are typed and validated at creation time to prevent opaque values entering the mesh.
resolution_summary: Rollback + temporary isolation stabilized routing. Permanent fixes target normalization, damping, telemetry, and publisher throttles. Owner teams have clear action items with deadlines; monitoring and a runbook update are in progress.
acceptance_criteria: Tag normalization merged and behind a feature flag; no routing hop regression in staging under 1M synthetic requests
Sticky-ttl damping implemented and verified to prevent immediate override across regions in controlled test
Dashboard alerts created and tested; on-call receives alerts for hop-count regressions
Runbook updated with rollback steps and verified in a game day
final_note: Will schedule a 30-minute follow-up review on 2026-03-25 to confirm all action items are complete and to decide on permanent enablement of normalization and damping changes. If any action slips, escalate to director of infra.
